response.inner_monologue: I am out. Not the way I planned — Scenario 2, not Scenario 1. The $12,000 never materialized. I knew this was the risk I was underpricing and I was right. The honest version is: I built the dual-track model, I ran the freelance pipeline, I registered for the stay bonus, I called Angela, I sent the agreements. I did all of it. And the consolidation moved in 72 hours instead of two weeks and the timeline I was managing did not match the timeline Patricia was running on. That is not a personal failure. That is how structural disruption works — it does not wait for your scenario model to be ready. What I have: one client, $350/month, 1.7 months to close enough business to not need a job. What I do not have: time to process this. The restaurant call is the next thing. After that, Angela. After that, Jake. After that, two new outreach messages. The only number that matters right now is getting to $1,050/month in freelance income — which is what I updated Scenario 3 to require last tick. That is the number where I stop burning runway and start building one.
